title: Pauli and Clifford Groups, Binary Symplectic Tableaux

items.title: Phase aware n qubit pauli group
items.statement:
The displayed tensor powers are tensor maps on the ordered factors, using [[def-qc-tensor-map]].
Fix an integer $n\ge 1$. Let $\mathcal H_n=Q_2^{\otimes n}$ be the ordered tensor register of $n$ qubits from [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], and let $\mathbb F_2=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. We name the wires $1,\ldots,n$; wire $j$ is position $j-1$ in the source's $0$-based factor list. Bit tuples use the big-endian encoding from [[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]], so the first wire is the most significant bit. Write $X_j$ and $Z_j$ for the tensor maps with the displayed one-qubit matrix on wire $j$ and the identity on every other wire. For $x,z\in\mathbb F_2^n$, set $X^x=\bigotimes_{j=1}^n X^{x_j}$ and $Z^z=\bigotimes_{j=1}^n Z^{z_j}$, where an exponent $0$ means the identity on that factor and an exponent $1$ means the displayed Pauli matrix. For $k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$, define

$$P(k,x,z):=i^kX^xZ^z.$$

The **phase-aware $n$-qubit Pauli set** $\mathcal P_n$ is the set of these operators with matrix multiplication. Its scalar subset is $Z_n:=\{i^k I_{\mathcal H_n}:k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z\}$. The product-and-adjoint theorem proves that $\mathcal P_n$ is a group and that $Z_n$ is its center.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes
John Preskill, Quantum Error Correction, Physics 229 Lecture Notes, Chapter 7

proof_obligations: define multiplication and identity conventions before using the group name.
items.axiom_use: None; this is a finite-dimensional definition.

items.title: Hadamard pauli action
items.statement: For a Hadamard gate $H_j$ on factor $j$, conjugation swaps the binary coordinates $x_j,z_j$ and changes the phase exactly by $2x_jz_j$ modulo $4$. In particular $HXH=Z$, $HZH=X$, and $HYH=-Y$.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes
John Watrous, Understanding Quantum Information and Computation, Lesson 14
Scott Aaronson and Daniel Gottesman, Improved Simulation of Stabilizer Circuits

proof_obligations: explicit matrix/conjugation computation.
items.axiom_use: None; the proof is a finite matrix and tensor calculation.

items.title: Phase gate pauli action
items.statement: For a phase gate $S_j=\operatorname{diag}(1,i)$ on factor $j$, the binary update is $(x_j,z_j)\mapsto(x_j,z_j+x_j)$ and the phase update is $k\mapsto k+x_j$ modulo $4$. In particular $SXS^*=Y$ and $SZS^*=Z$.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes
John Watrous, Understanding Quantum Information and Computation, Lesson 14
Scott Aaronson and Daniel Gottesman, Improved Simulation of Stabilizer Circuits

proof_obligations: explicit matrix calculation consistent with item 3’s phase convention.
items.axiom_use: None; the proof is a finite matrix and tensor calculation.

items.title: Pauli product and adjoint
items.statement:
For $k,k'\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$ and $x,z,x',z'\in\mathbb F_2^n$, with $P(k,x,z)=i^kX^xZ^z$ and $X^xZ^z$ ordered as written,

$$P(k,x,z)P(k',x',z')=P(k+k'+2(z\cdot x'),x+x',z+z'),$$

where the dot product is first evaluated in $\mathbb F_2$ as $0$ or $1$, and then multiplied by $2$ in $\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$. The set $\mathcal P_n$ is a group. If $p\in\{0,1\}$ represents $x\cdot z\in\mathbb F_2$, then $P(k,x,z)^*=P(2p-k,x,z)=P(k,x,z)^{-1}$, and its center is $Z_n=\{i^k I:k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z\}$.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes
John Preskill, Quantum Error Correction, Physics 229 Lecture Notes, Chapter 7
Scott Aaronson and Daniel Gottesman, Improved Simulation of Stabilizer Circuits

proof_obligations: commute Zᶻ past Xˣ′ and track the scalar i power, including the integer representative of the parity bit.
items.axiom_use: None; all arguments are finite tensor and matrix calculations.

items.title: Binary Pauli label and quotient
items.statement:
Let $Z_n$ be the scalar center of $\mathcal P_n$. Define $P\sim Q$ when $P^{-1}Q\in Z_n$, and let $Q_n$ be the set of equivalence classes $[P]=PZ_n$. The proposed coset product is $[P][Q]=[PQ]$. The quotient theorem verifies this product is well-defined and proves that the assignment

$$\lambda:Q_n\longrightarrow V_n:=\mathbb F_2^n\oplus\mathbb F_2^n,\qquad [P(k,x,z)]\longmapsto(x,z)$$

is a group isomorphism to the additive group of $V_n$. A binary label deliberately forgets the scalar phase.

references.title: John Preskill, Quantum Error Correction, Physics 229 Lecture Notes, Chapter 7
M. Hein et al., Entanglement in Graph States and Its Applications

proof_obligations: show the map is well-defined, onto, a homomorphism, and has exactly the scalar center as kernel.
items.axiom_use: None; this is a finite quotient construction.

items.title: Clifford normalizer
items.statement:
Work with actual unitary matrices, not equivalence classes modulo global phase. The $n$-qubit **Clifford normalizer** is

$$\mathcal C_n:=\{U\text{ unitary on }\mathcal H_n:U\mathcal P_nU^*=\mathcal P_n\}.$$

It is a group under matrix multiplication. Every scalar unitary $\lambda I$ with $|\lambda|=1$ belongs to $\mathcal C_n$ and has the same conjugation action as $I$; the chosen convention retains these distinct matrices.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes
John Watrous, Understanding Quantum Information and Computation, Lesson 14

proof_obligations: verify closure under products/inverses and distinguish global scalar phase from Pauli center.
items.axiom_use: None; group closure follows from finite matrix multiplication and unitary inverses.

items.title: CNOT Pauli action
items.statement:
Let $n\ge2$ and let distinct $c,t\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$ be control and target indices. For CNOT $C_{c\to t}$ acting on $y\in\mathbb F_2^n$ by toggling coordinate $t$ by $y_c$, conjugation sends

$$P(k,x,z)\longmapsto P(k,x',z'),\qquad x'_t=x_t+x_c,\quad z'_c=z_c+z_t,$$

with all other coordinates unchanged and additions in $\mathbb F_2$. In particular, $X_c\mapsto X_cX_t$, $Z_c\mapsto Z_c$, $X_t\mapsto X_t$, and $Z_t\mapsto Z_cZ_t$; the phase coordinate $k$ is unchanged in the fixed $X^xZ^z$ order.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes
M. Hein et al., Entanglement in Graph States and Its Applications
Scott Aaronson and Daniel Gottesman, Improved Simulation of Stabilizer Circuits

proof_obligations: calculate images on the four generators and extend using item 3.
items.axiom_use: None; the gate rules are finite basis and matrix calculations.

items.title: Hermitian Pauli phase criterion
items.statement: For $P(k,x,z)=i^kX^xZ^z\in\mathcal P_n$, the operator is Hermitian exactly when $k\equiv x\cdot z\pmod 2$. In that case $P(k,x,z)^2=I$.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes
John Watrous, Understanding Quantum Information and Computation, Lesson 14

proof_obligations: compute the adjoint under the fixed Xᶻ ordering.
items.axiom_use: None; the proof uses the finite phase-aware product law.

items.title: Binary symplectic form
items.statement:
On $V_n=\mathbb F_2^n\oplus\mathbb F_2^n$, with coordinate order $(x,z)$, define

$$\omega((x,z),(x',z')):=x\cdot z'+z\cdot x'.$$

This is a nondegenerate alternating bilinear form over $\mathbb F_2$; $V_n$ has dimension $2n$. In characteristic two, alternating also implies symmetry.

references.title: John Preskill, Quantum Error Correction, Physics 229 Lecture Notes, Chapter 7
M. Hein et al., Entanglement in Graph States and Its Applications

proof_obligations: check bilinearity and alternation in characteristic two; prove nondegeneracy by testing coordinate vectors. Optional supplier: thm-alternating-forms-have-a-symplectic-normal-form.
items.axiom_use: None; all claims follow by finite coordinate calculations.

items.title: Binary Pauli quotient isomorphism
items.statement: The map $\pi:\mathcal P_n\to V_n$, $P(k,x,z)\mapsto(x,z)$, is a surjective group homomorphism with kernel exactly $Z_n$. Therefore the quotient map in [[def-qc-binary-pauli-label-and-quotient]] is an isomorphism $\mathcal P_n/Z_n\cong (V_n,+)$, and $\dim_{\mathbb F_2}V_n=2n$. No phase or label ambiguity occurs, including when $n=1$.

references.title: John Preskill, Quantum Error Correction, Physics 229 Lecture Notes, Chapter 7
M. Hein et al., Entanglement in Graph States and Its Applications
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes

proof_obligations: Prove exact Pauli label uniqueness up to scalar using ordered computational-basis vectors.
Use the phase-aware multiplication law to prove homomorphism, kernel, surjectivity, and dimension, including n=1.
items.axiom_use: None; surjectivity, injectivity, and dimension use explicit finite coordinates.

items.title: Phase-aware binary Clifford tableau
items.statement:
Fix the generator order $X_1,\ldots,X_n,Z_1,\ldots,Z_n$ and label order $(x,z)$, with wire indices as in [[def-qc-phase-aware-n-qubit-pauli-group]]. For an actual Clifford unitary $U\in\mathcal C_n$, write each exact generator image uniquely as

$$UX_jU^*=P(k_j,x_j,z_j),\qquad UZ_jU^*=P(k_{n+j},x_{n+j},z_{n+j}).$$

Its **phase-aware binary Clifford tableau** is the pair $(S,p)$, where $S\in M_{2n}(\mathbb F_2)$ has as its ordered columns the $2n$ labels $(x_j,z_j)$ just listed and $p=(k_1,\ldots,k_{2n})\in(\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z)^{2n}$. The phase vector retains the exact mod-$4$ generator-image phases; it is not discarded with the binary labels. The columns define the unique linear map on $V_n$ taking the ordered standard basis to those columns. Only pairs arising from a Clifford are called Clifford tableaux; arbitrary binary matrices and phase vectors need not be valid. A scalar global phase on $U$ does not change its tableau.

references.title: Scott Aaronson and Daniel Gottesman, Improved Simulation of Stabilizer Circuits
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes
John Watrous, Understanding Quantum Information and Computation, Lesson 14

proof_obligations: Fix generator and wire order explicitly.
Keep exact mod-4 phases distinct from the binary label block.
items.axiom_use: None; the tableau records finitely many exact generator images.

items.title: Clifford circuits lift binary symplectic transvections
items.statement: For every nonzero $v=(x,z)\in V_n$, the transvection $\tau_v(w)=w+\omega(w,v)v$ is induced on binary Pauli labels by an explicit Clifford circuit made from local $H$, $S$, $S^*$, CNOT, and wire swaps. Its mod-$4$ phase lift is computed by applying the exact gate update rules in sequence; no phase coordinate is suppressed.

references.title: M. Hein et al., Entanglement in Graph States and Its Applications
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes

proof_obligations: construct a local Clifford circuit sending any nonzero Hermitian Pauli to Z_1
conjugate the S_1 lift and track every phase update
items.axiom_use: None; each circuit and reduction is finite and uses no choice principle.

items.title: Symplectic transvections generate the binary symplectic group
items.statement: Let $V$ be any finite-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb F_2$ with a nondegenerate alternating form $\omega$, and let $\dim V=2n$. Call an invertible linear map $T:V\to V$ **symplectic** when $\omega(Tu,Tw)=\omega(u,w)$ for all $u,w\in V$. For each $v\in V$, define the transvection $\tau_v(w)=w+\omega(w,v)v$. Every symplectic map is a finite composition of these transvections. The form on $V_n$ from [[def-qc-binary-symplectic-form]] is the application needed here. This is a choice-free finite-dimensional reduction.

references.title: M. Hein et al., Entanglement in Graph States and Its Applications
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes

proof_obligations: prove transvections are symplectic involutions
prove transitivity on nonzero vectors and the stabilizer reduction
induct on n using the orthogonal complement
items.axiom_use: None; the reduction uses finite-dimensional linear algebra and finite induction, with no choice principle.

items.title: Pauli commutator is symplectic pairing
items.statement:
For $a=(x,z)$ and $b=(x',z')$ in $V_n$ and any phases $k,k'$, 

$$P(k,x,z)P(k',x',z')=(-1)^{\omega(a,b)}P(k',x',z')P(k,x,z).$$

Thus the Pauli operators commute exactly when their labels are symplectically orthogonal.

references.title: John Preskill, Quantum Error Correction, Physics 229 Lecture Notes, Chapter 7
M. Hein et al., Entanglement in Graph States and Its Applications
Scott Aaronson and Daniel Gottesman, Improved Simulation of Stabilizer Circuits

proof_obligations: compare the two exact phase-aware products; binary labels alone do not prove signed group identities.
items.axiom_use: None; the proof compares the finite phase-aware products.

items.title: Clifford induces symplectic map
items.statement: For each $U\in\mathcal C_n$, conjugation induces an invertible $\mathbb F_2$-linear map $S_U:V_n\to V_n$ satisfying $\omega(S_Ua,S_Ub)=\omega(a,b)$ for all $a,b\in V_n$. Thus $S_U$ is symplectic. The assignment respects multiplication: $S_{UV}=S_U\circ S_V$ for all $U,V\in\mathcal C_n$.

references.title: M. Hein et al., Entanglement in Graph States and Its Applications
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes
John Preskill, Quantum Error Correction, Physics 229 Lecture Notes, Chapter 7

proof_obligations: show conjugation descends through the scalar quotient and is invertible
derive linearity and preservation of the commutator pairing
items.axiom_use: None; conjugation and the quotient action use finite-dimensional algebra only.

items.title: Clifford to binary symplectic action is surjective
items.statement: For every $n\ge1$, write $\operatorname{Sp}(V_n,\omega)$ for the group of invertible $\mathbb F_2$-linear maps $T:V_n\to V_n$ satisfying $\omega(Ta,Tb)=\omega(a,b)$ for all $a,b$. For every $T\in\operatorname{Sp}(V_n,\omega)$ there is a Clifford circuit $U$ made from Hadamard gates $H$, phase gates $S,S^*$, CNOT, and wire swaps whose induced action on binary Pauli labels is $T$. Since the phase gate satisfies $S^*=S^3$, this group is also generated by $H$, $S$, CNOT, and swaps. Hence the conjugation homomorphism from the Clifford normalizer to $\operatorname{Sp}(V_n,\omega)$ is onto. The proof uses finite transvection reduction and exact mod-$4$ phase updates at every gate.

references.title: M. Hein et al., Entanglement in Graph States and Its Applications
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes
John Watrous, Understanding Quantum Information and Computation, Lesson 14

proof_obligations: prove transvection generation by finite symplectic reduction
give an explicit Clifford circuit lifting each transvection and track mod-4 phases
items.axiom_use: None; the decomposition and synthesis use finite induction, not arbitrary choice.

title: Pauli and Clifford Groups, Binary Symplectic Tableaux — Examples

items.title: Pauli commutator and binary symplectic sign
items.statement: For one qubit, the labels of $X$ and $Z$ have symplectic pairing $1$, so the binary form records their anticommutation. The two operators $Z$ and $-Z$ have the same binary label but different mod-$4$ phases.

references.title: John Preskill, Quantum Error Correction, Physics 229 Lecture Notes, Chapter 7
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes

proof_obligations: Use the phase-aware product law and compute the binary alternating form.
items.axiom_use: None; the example is a direct one-qubit matrix calculation.
